The system replaces traditional monetary indicators with the L-Axis Flux Engine (LFE), a four-module architecture (ETV, PCS, DTM, SPLM) that operates on tension-flow mechanics rather than financial metrics. The C-Axis gravitational architecture (IFT, SNSV, PRL, SLIP, AIT) defines the internal thresholds through which tension accumulates, reflects, separates, and ignites. At its apex, the EPA Activation Layer (EAL) introduces Elasticity of Perceived Abundance , a mechanism absent from all existing economic, psychological, and systemic models. UNC System L is the first architecture to treat perception as a structural variable capable of generating economic reality.

title: Rethinking Value with Modern Monetary Theory: Toward a Reconstruction of Economics through Dynamic Approach

detail.title: Rethinking Value with Modern Monetary Theory: Toward a Reconstruction of Economics through Dynamic Approach
detail.abstract: This paper takes an initial step toward reconstructing a theory of value consistent with Modern Monetary Theory, offering an alternative to the utility theory of value. By analyzing the arguments of its proponents, we confirm that the currently dominant utility theory of value relies on static models and assumes the existence of "moments in which all exchanges are completed simultaneously." The unrealistic nature of this assumption has rarely been questioned; however, it not only impedes the proper integration of money into the theoretical framework but also leads to significant differences in the conclusions of exchange theory. In response, this paper proposes a new theory of value that incorporates a dynamic aspect, explicitly reflecting the characteristics of a market economy in which exchanges occur continuously. Furthermore, within the framework of this new value theory, we propose marginal expected utility analysis that extends the conventional marginal utility analysis into a dynamic setting. We examine its applicability to the real economy through both a commodity market model and a government-issued public money model. The results are broadly consistent with the claims of Modern Monetary Theory and Post-Keynesian economics, including markup pricing theory and the tax-driven money view. Moreover, by modeling firms as price-setters rather than price-takers, we theoretically derive realistic price-adjustment processes in disequilibrium markets without relying on ad hoc assumptions. These findings indicate that accurately capturing the dynamics of continuous market exchanges is essential for reconstructing the theory of value and exchange.

Korean Abstract: 
수도권 인구집중 추세는 1970년대 이래 반전 없이 지속되고 있다. 2010년대의 경우, 수도권의 반도체 및 지식기반 산업 생산성 증가와 비수도권 제조업 도시의 생산성 감소가 추세를 주도하였다. 세종시 등 신도시 건설은 인프라 투자에 치중하여 생산성 증가가 제한적이었고, 인구 유입 촉진에도 한계를 보였다. 균형발전을 위해서는 인프라 투자를 넘어 지역의 생산성을 제고해야 한다. 또한 수도권-비수도권 격차를 줄이고자 한다면 비수도권 내의 격차를 일정 정도 용인할 필요가 있다.

English Abstract: 
Population concentration in the Seoul Metropolitan Area has continued unabated since the 1970s. In the 2010s, diverging productivity drove this trend—gains in semiconductor and knowledge-based sectors in the capital region versus losses in manufacturing-oriented regional cities. Planned city projects, including Sejong, heavily prioritized infrastructure provision, yielding limited productivity growth and only modest population inflows. To achieve balanced development, spatial policy should move beyond infrastructure investment to boosting regional productivity. Furthermore, narrowing the divide between the capital region and outer regions may necessitate accepting some disparities within outer areas.

Korean Abstract: 
스케일업 기업은 경제에 새로운 활력을 불어넣고 국가경쟁력을 강화하는 데 핵심적인 역할을 한다. 이들 기업은 신산업 분야에서 디지털 전환, 친환경 기술, 신재생 에너지 등과 같은 혁신을 선도하며, 산업구조 변화를 가속화하고 지속가능한 성장을 이끄는 동력으로 작용한다. 이러한 측면에서 스케일업 기업의 성장을 촉진하는 최적의 생태계를 조성하고, 고성장 기업이 지속적으로 배출될 수 있는 환경을 마련하는 것은 국가경쟁력을 강화하는 데 중요한 역할을 할 수 있다. 그러나 현실적으로 우리나라의 많은 기업들이 스케일업 과정에서 적합한 인재 확보, 디지털 도구의 효과적 활용, 연구개발 협력, 글로벌 시장 진출 등 다양한 장벽에 직면하고 있다.

본 연구는 우리나라 기업 생태계가 혁신적이고 경쟁력 있는 기업들에 대해 국내 시장은 물론 글로벌 시장에서도 지속적으로 성장할 수 있는 환경을 제공하고 있는지 점검한다. 그리고 그러한 환경을 충분히 제공하지 못한 부분에 집중하여, 보다 바람직한 생태계로 전환하기 위한 정책방향과 실행전략을 제시한다. 연구는 총 4개의 주요 장으로 구성되어 있다. 이하 문단에서는 각 장에서 다루는 주요 내용을 제2장부터 제5장까지 순차적으로 요약한다.

English Abstract: 
Scale-up firms play a pivotal role in injecting new vitality into the economy and enhancing national competitiveness. Given the stagnant growth potential, it is increasingly important to create an ecosystem optimized for scale-up firms to grow and to establish an environment where high-growth firms can continuously emerge. However, in reality, many firms in Korea face various barriers during the scale-up process, including difficulties in securing skilled talent, utilizing digital tools, and expanding into global markets.

In response, this study examines whether Korea’s business ecosystem provides an environment where innovative and competitive firms can continuously grow beyond the domestic market into the global market. And by focusing on areas where such an environment is insufficiently provided, it presents policy directions and implementation strategies for transitioning to a more desirable ecosystem.

Consisting of four main chapters, the study emphasizes the following policy suggestions. First, as the decline in the proportion of high-growth firms weakens economic dynamism and job creation, the government must shift toward scale-up policies and establish an integrated management system to support these firms. Second, to enhance the global competitiveness of startups, it is essential to introduce a specialized visa focusing on innovation and growth potential, streamline permanent residency pathways, and expand tax benefits. Third, to encourage firms to pursue sustained growth in export markets, it is necessary to design export promotion programs that are performance-based and tied to their success in export markets. Fourth, revitalizing industry-academia-research collaboration requires a demand-driven policy approach, increased participation from large and mid-sized firms, patent box incentives, and strengthened industry linkages with public research institutes.

Despite increasing risk exposure from expanding assets and leverage among large securities firms, the current Net Capital Ratio (NCR) framework does not adequately capture these risks. To strengthen risk sensitivity while maintaining a balance between financial soundness and industry growth, the NCR formula for large securities firms should revert to its pre-2016 structure, and a differentiated regulatory approach tailored to business scope and risk characteristics should apply to small- and medium-sized firms.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a structural interpretation of primitive selection and strategic node resonance within high-pressure institutional, economic, informational, and energetic architectures. It argues that large systems do not elevate individuals based on competence, ideology, or intentional design, but through compatibility with the system's dominant tension field. Primitive selection is conceptualized not as a psychological or moral phenomenon, but as a structural adaptation emerging from unresolved internal geometry. When institutional coherence weakens, when informational fields fragment, and when resource flows generate irregular energetic pressure (EPA Pulse), systems begin to favor operators whose cognitive and behavioral profiles match the frequency of systemic discharge. The analysis introduces the Tourbillon Cognitive Mechanism, a rotational architecture that explains how tension circulates, reflects, and amplifies across layers. Through the interaction between Pulse, rotation, and reflection, systems generate the illusion of intentional destabilization. In reality, destabilization is a by-product of rhythmic irregularities within the architecture. The paper demonstrates that weak strategic nodesdefined not by their visible function but by their positional intersection of flows-act as amplification points for systemic tension. When such nodes lose coherence, tension no longer distributes evenly; it propagates, accelerates, and projects outward, producing global resonance effects independent of deliberate action. UNC sYstEm L is presented as an integrative architectural mechanism capable of stabilizing high-pressure systems by recalibrating Pulse, re-anchoring strategic nodes, and redistributing tension across the structural field. Rather than intervening on individuals or institutional actors, the mechanism operates on geometry: rotation, alignment, continuity, and axial tension. The framework demonstrates that systemic stabilization can be achieved without ideological intervention, political competition, or coercive restructuring. Instead, continuity emerges from restoring rhythm, coherence, and structural alignment. This paper contributes a unified analytical model that integrates institutional dynamics, economic flows, informational fragmentation, and energetic pressure into a single architectural framework. It reframes destabilization as a structural phenomenon driven by rhythm rather than intention, and offers a non-reductionist method for interpreting how systems generate their own operators under pressure. The findings have implications for institutional design, risk analysis, cognitive architecture, and the study of systemic resilience in high-field environments.

title: The Happiness Crash of 2020

detail.title: The Happiness Crash of 2020

detail.abstract: I document a sudden, sharp and historically unprecedented decline in self-reported happiness in the US population. It occurred during 2020, the year of the Covid pandemic, and mainly persists through 2024. This happiness crash spread across nearly all typical demographics and geographies. The happiest groups pre-Covid (e.g., whites, high income, well-educated and politically/ideologically right-leaning) tend to show the largest happiness reductions. The glaring exception is marital status, which has consistently been an important marker for happiness. The already wide happiness premium for marriage has, if anything, become slightly wider. With both married and unmarried reporting large declines in happiness the country has become segregated: slightly over half-the married adults-remain happy on balance; the unmarried, nearly half, are now distinctly unhappy. I also show that across a number of aspects of personal and social capital post-Covid deterioration is the norm, including a collapse of belief in the fairness of others and of trust in the US Supreme Court.

detail.abstract: Anthropogenic climate change is speeding up the world's hydrological cycle, making the old dichotomies of "drought relief" and "flood defense" obsolete. This study examines the Flood-Drought Abrupt Alternation (DFAA) and Flood-Drought Continuum concepts, contending that integrating these two phenomena through Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) and Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) is essential to ensuring global water security. Overflowing floodwater can be used to alleviate drought scarcity through the use of "Managed Aquifer Recharge" (MAR) and data-driven forecasting. In order to suggest a single governance framework that views water as a single resource rather than a divided risk, this study synthesizes international case studies from the SADC region, California, and India.

title: Escalation Without Enforcement: Hidden Grace Periods in Tiered Bank Supervision
affiliations: New York University School of Law

detail.title: Escalation Without Enforcement: Hidden Grace Periods in Tiered Bank Supervision
detail.abstract:
Forthcoming in the Journal of Banking Regulation.

Silicon Valley Bank's March 2023 failure exposes a structural tension in size-tiered bank supervision: the same portfolio framework designed to escalate prudential expectations can also create hidden grace periods that delay binding constraint. Using SVB's transition from the Federal Reserve's Regional Banking Organization program to the Large and Foreign Banking Organization program, this article traces how phased-in enhanced prudential standards, waiver-delayed ratings, and the internal classification of supervisory findings combined to produce a long supervisory runway during which liquidity, interest-rate, and governance weaknesses were repeatedly identified but not decisively constrained. The article treats tiering as a dual-use institutional technology: it reallocates supervisory resources and raises formal requirements, yet it also embeds transitional mechanisms that make deferral the path of least resistance. A public-choice account links that deferral to internal coordination costs, signaling concerns, and the limited legal status of supervisory guidance. The analysis is institutional rather than firm-specific and highlights why long runways are most dangerous when rapidly growing banks exhibit observable deterioration that can compound before formal intervention becomes unavoidable.

title: Breaking the HISCO Barrier: Automatic Occupational Standardization with OccCANINE

detail.title: Breaking the HISCO Barrier: Automatic Occupational Standardization with OccCANINE
detail.abstract: This paper introduces OccCANINE, an open-source tool that maps occupational descriptions to HISCO codes. Manual coding is slow and error-prone; OccCANINE replaces weeks of work with results in minutes. We fine-tune CANINE on 15.8 million description-code pairs from 29 sources in 13 languages. The model achieves 96 percent accuracy, precision, and recall. We also show that the approach generalizes to three systems - OCC1950, OCCICEM, and ISCO-68 - and release them open source. By breaking the "HISCO barrier," OccCANINE democratizes access to high-quality occupational coding, enabling broader research in economics, economic history, and related disciplines.

title: Homeowners Associations, Reserve Funding, and Condominium Maintenance: Evidence from Florida

detail.title: Homeowners Associations, Reserve Funding, and Condominium Maintenance: Evidence from Florida
detail.abstract: Condominium maintenance requires collective saving for predictable capital expenditures. I study Florida's 2022 SB 4-D law, which mandates structural reserve funding and milestone inspections for condominium buildings. Difference-indifferences estimates show that the law raised HOA fees by 4.9-6.8 percent and permit probabilities by about 1.4-3.9 percentage points, indicating that real maintenance spending had been deferred. I then construct an association-level measure of reserve-adjustment intensity, delta_i, to study heterogeneity in market responses to reserve catch-up. Delta-on-delta regressions show that a one-standard-deviation larger reserve adjustment is associated with roughly 2-3 percentage points more negative price growth. Capitalization timing tests further show that the price-level discount widens progressively from the pre-period through 2025, with high-delta_i associations showing about 7 percent lower listed prices in levels by 2025. Because reduced-form event studies show little broad price response, I interpret these results as heterogeneous repricing around reserve needs rather than a uniform decline. Relative to full mechanical capitalization of the fee increase as net new cost, the estimated price response is much smaller in magnitude. Larger fee growth is also associated with more assessment liens against unit owners, and suggestive cross-sectional evidence points to financial capacity rather than association complexity as a driver of reserve underfunding.

declarations.ethicsApproval: The survey experiment has been pre-registered at the AEA RCT Registry under number AEARCTR-0016068, https://doi.org/10.1257/rct.16068-1.0 and received the ethics approval from ETH Zurich under number 25 ETHICS-161.

detail.abstract: We study how firms’ expectations respond to prospective tariff shocks using a randomized survey experiment among Swiss manufacturing firms. When confronted with potential U.S. tariffs, respondents expect sizable declines in turnover and investment yet anticipate increases in ex-tariff export prices despite falling demand. This combination of declining activity and rising prices runs counter to the standard prediction of trade models, in which tariffs reduce foreign demand and put downward pressure on exporters’ prices. The observed pattern is consistent with a destination-specific cost-push mechanism, whereby tariffs raise exporters’ marginal costs through compliance burdens, logistical frictions, or reduced scale. Embedding firms stated price and sales expectations in a parsimonious structural pricing model, we quantify the implied cost changes and recover sector-level demand elasticities. The estimates indicate substantial heterogeneity across industries and are, on average, consistent with short-run trade elasticities from the recent literature. Moreover, we corroborate the experimental evidence using panel survey data on firms’ expectations around an unexpected U.S. tariff announcement.

detail.abstract: AI-enabled automation is reshaping production, services, and knowledge work, bringing real concerns about displacement, deskilling, and the concentration of decision power in opaque systems. At the same time, research in human-AI interaction, human-in-the-loop (HITL) methods, and explainable AI (XAI) shows that AI can be designed to augment human capabilities and support work practices that are more equitable and trustworthy. Existing work, however, tends to focus on interaction patterns and system-level governance, while leaving the design of jobs, skills, and certification pathways under-specified. This paper introduces the concept of human-in-the-loop labor architectures: socio-technical configurations in which HITL and XAI capabilities are deliberately used to reinstate and reconfigure jobs, define new skill profiles, and anchor certification and policy interventions. We propose a four-layer framework-capabilities, roles, skills and certification, and governance-that connects AI affordances to occupational structures and institutional arrangements. Drawing on research on AI and the future of work, human-centered AI, and organisational fairness, we show how this architecture can reinstate and upgrade roles in automation, human resources, collaboration, and well-being, and how governments and institutions can use it to elevate human capabilities and quality of life in an evolving global economy.

detail.abstract: The persistent gap between strategic formulation and operational execution remains a primary challenge for modern enterprises and continues to erode a substantial share of potential value creation. V.M. Benignus Grero's Strategic Value Architecture (SVA) methodology is a practitioner-developed, architectural approach designed to address this "strategy-execution gap", conceptualized as a systemic "Value Gap" between strategic intent and realized outcomes. SVA is built on three interconnected pillars-a Value Capture Model using algebraically constrained KPI trees, a Competitive Advantage Model structured around strategic flywheels and Hamilton Helmer's 7 Powers, and a Value Delivery Model focused on quantifiable customer outcomes-integrated through an AI-supported synthesis layer. This paper situates SVA within established research on performance measurement (MBO, CSFs, BSC, OKRs), value creation, value capture, value delivery, and strategic and enterprise architecture. It critically examines the terminology, novelty, and prior art surrounding key components, including Bernie Smith's KPI Trees and component-based business model patents, and clarifies how SVA reframes and integrates these concepts. The analysis finds that SVA's primary contribution lies not in the invention of isolated concepts but in its holistic architectural synthesis: the insistence on algebraic KPI relationships, the explicit coupling of competitive advantage mechanisms to measurable drivers, and the use of AI to manage systemic complexity within a unified management methodology. The paper concludes by outlining assumptions and limitations of SVA and proposing avenues for empirical research to test its claimed performance impacts in diverse organizational contexts.

detail.abstract: The future of antitrust and consumer protection law in the United States is being reshaped by digitalization, rising market concentration, and the dominance of large technology platforms, all of which strain traditional doctrines built around price and consumer surplus. The paper argues that current U.S. antitrust enforcement has become too narrow and outdated, focusing mainly on short‑run price effects while underestimating harms from increased market power, common ownership, exclusionary conduct, data exploitation, and platform‑driven constraints on user choice and autonomy. It reviews how existing law treats efficiency defenses, merger control, and monopsony harms, and shows that many anticompetitive mergers, cartels, and tacit collusion escape effective scrutiny, especially in data‑driven and network‑effect‑heavy markets. Using examples from dominant online platforms, the study highlights how business models that monetize user data, restrict interoperability, and leverage “essential facilities” can damage competition, innovation, and non‑price dimensions of consumer welfare. The paper concludes that U.S. antitrust and consumer protection law should be modernized by shifting from a narrow consumer‑surplus lens to a broader total‑welfare and multi‑dimensional consumer‑welfare standard, strengthening enforcement against exclusionary digital conduct, revitalizing doctrines such as essential facilities, and explicitly accounting for data, privacy, and non‑price harms in the assessment of market power and mergers.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the integrated dataset developed by the National Observatory of Inter-firm Networks (ONRI) to analyse the structure and evolution of business network contracts in Italy. The dataset combines multiple sources of information, including administrative records from the Italian Business Register (InfoCamere), firm-level economic and financial data from the AIDA database, and original survey data collected through repeated waves. The survey is structured as a longitudinal instrument, with four waves conducted in 2019, 2021, 2023, and 2025. It includes a set of overlapping questions that ensure comparability over time, alongside thematic modules addressing key aspects of network activity, such as access to credit, start-ups, financial and labor-related dimensions, and human capital. By integrating network-level and firm-level information, the dataset offers a comprehensive framework for analysing governance mechanisms, organizational structures, and performance dynamics of business networks. The paper provides a methodological guide to the dataset and is intended to support researchers, practitioners, and policymakers interested in the study and development of inter-firm collaboration.

detail.abstract:
Law restricts the exercise of a sovereign’s raw power not only by forbidding certain conduct or outcomes, but also by choreographing the sequence through which sovereign acts are considered, authorized, and executed. International Humanitarian Law (IHL) offers a particularly clear illustration. At its doctrinal core, IHL is a law of process: it structures how belligerent parties move from intelligence collection to military operations, from operations to particular attacks and strikes, and from those attacks back into renewed cycles of intelligence gathering and analysis. By organizing military decision-making around a set of sequential stages, IHL creates intervals for review, consultation, and supervision—moments in which principals can meaningfully oversee the actions of their agents.

In this sense, the law of targeting is best understood as a law of temporal friction. Commanders review the recommendations of subordinates, consult legal advisors, and transmit assessments upward to the political echelon. Each step introduces delay that invites  deliberation. Much the same can be said of the “law of intelligence,” which may likewise be understood as a law of temporal friction. The intelligence cycle—through which raw collection becomes analysis, analysis becomes intelligence products, and those products are disseminated to decision-makers—is itself structured around a set of choreographed pauses. These pauses enable the verification of sources, the reassessment of hypotheses, and ultimately the capacity to resist and object to premature action. Temporal friction, in other words, mitigates the principal–agent problems that arise when predictive and analytic functions are delegated to subordinate units.

The integration of artificial intelligence into wartime decision-making fundamentally alters both the pace and the character of military and intelligence operations. Automation compresses the progression from data collection and analysis to operational exploitation and military response. This chapter examines the current and emerging landscape of AI-enabled digital surveillance in kinetic and cyber warfare, with particular attention to its implications under both IHL and international human rights law (IHRL). It argues that such systems are designed to erode temporal friction, rendering existing legal constraints both harder to operationalize and easier to circumvent. By collapsing the intervals of judgment that once mediated the movement from perception to action, AI displaces the very temporal structure through which law exerts control. This dynamic is especially visible in situations of belligerent occupation, where the automation of surveillance and administrative governance risks transforming what is formally a temporary, legally bounded military presence into a durable, algorithmically sustained permanent condition of hostility. The chapter concludes by assessing ways to restore that friction, whether through institutional design or technical architecture, as a mode of ensuring that legality may endure in the face of automation.

detail.title: The Regulatory Intermediation Gap: Evidence from Singapore's Equity Market Reform

publicationDetails.journalName: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: When governments channel equity market interventions through private intermediaries, the institutional architecture of intermediation systematically redirects those interventions away from their intended beneficiaries. Using a cross-sectional event study of firms listed on the Singapore Exchange (SGX), we examine Singapore's 2025 equity market reform (a S$5 billion capital deployment through professional fund managers bundled with deregulation of SGX's post-listing oversight regime) and document two dimensions of this regulatory intermediation gap. First, the market priced capital deployment as a large-cap event: the smallest quartile lost 2.1 percent while the largest gained 0.6 percent, consistent with fund managers' investability constraints that effectively exclude small firms. When mandate terms requiring small-and mid-cap allocation were later disclosed, the size gradient reversed, indicating that precise mandate design can narrow the gap. Second, the market penalised firms with accumulated regulatory friction (prior queries, halts, and suspensions), interpreting the proposed shift from public to private oversight as information loss. Yet previously watchlisted firms gained 8.1 percent upon abolition of the watch-list, revealing a dual-edged signal whose interpretation depends on financial condition. Both findings are instances of a single phenomenon: policy transmitted through institutional channels is shaped by those channels' constraints. The results inform the design of government-intermediated equity programmes in Singapore and comparable initiatives in Japan, Korea, and the European Union.

detail.abstract:
This dissertation consists of three chapters that study the measurement of household welfare, focusing on intrahousehold allocation and economies of scale to consumption.

The first chapter studies resource shares---the shares of total household expenditure attributed to each household member---which are key parameters of collective household models and capture the intrahousehold distribution of consumption. They are typically identified and estimated in the context of a small continuous demand system. This chapter extends the collective household model to a random utility framework, following Lanier et al. (2023) to estimate sparse demand systems. I provide a model wherein resource shares may be identified using extremely high-dimensional data, and I provide a consistent and asymptotically normal estimator. The estimation leverages techniques from machine learning to improve computational feasibility and efficiency. Using data from the United States from 2004 to 2020 provided by NielsenIQ, I estimate resource shares for people in a variety of household compositions. The results indicate no significant gender inequality in resource shares between adults, and suggest that adult men's and women's resource shares are slightly positively related to the household budget.

The second and third chapters, co-authored with Dr. Arthur Lewbel and Dr. Krishna Pendakur, study household economies of scale to consumption. Building on Browning et al. (2013), who model economies of scale by allowing goods to be partially shared rather than strictly private or public, the second chapter develops a theoretical framework that delivers simple point identification of good-specific economies of scale and proposes a new index of household-level economies of scale. The model is linear, accommodates households of varying compositions, including children, and allows for unobserved heterogeneity in both preferences and good-specific economies of scale. The third chapter develops the estimation strategy for this framework and provides a step-by-step procedure for estimating the distribution of economies-of-scale parameters. We then present empirical estimates using data from the Canadian Survey of Household Spending and find little joint consumption of goods by children and adults, as well as limited unobserved heterogeneity in economies of scale across households with the same composition.

title: Words Matter When Gangs Cyberbang: Predicting Imminent Urban Violence from Gang Members’ Social Media Posts

detail.title: Words Matter When Gangs Cyberbang: Predicting Imminent Urban Violence from Gang Members’ Social Media Posts
detail.abstract: The rise in violent crime across major U.S. cities, fueled mainly by gang members using social media to broadcast messages of loss and aggression, poses an urgent challenge. Although prior research has examined gang-affiliated social media content, there remains a crucial gap in identifying which posts serve as credible signals of impending violence. Addressing this gap is essential for enhancing community safety, improving resource allocation, and optimizing law enforcement strategies. This study introduces a novel research model grounded in a contextualized adaptation of signaling theory. The model identifies key indicators of credible signals, such as follower count, specific hashtags, and retweet counts, which correlate with gang-related aggression. Environmental factors, such as temperature, are also examined for their influence on violent crime escalation. Using this contextualized theory, we designed a machine learning model to predict violent crime counts, training it on a dataset of 143,700 gang-affiliated tweets and their accompanying text and metadata. This approach enables automated identification of credible social media signals related to gang violence. The findings contribute to theory and practice by offering new insights into social media credibility and its link to violent crime, and by demonstrating how such signals can be used for prediction. Furthermore, the predictive model provides law enforcement with advanced tools to anticipate crime and inform community-based prevention strategies and policy development.

title: Set Shaping Theory Applied to Graphs: Reducing Average Graph Entropy via Dimensional Expansion

detail.title: Set Shaping Theory Applied to Graphs: Reducing Average Graph Entropy via Dimensional Expansion
detail.abstract: Set Shaping Theory (SST) introduces a compression paradigm that does not begin by encoding an object inside its original representation space. Instead, SST seeks a bijective transformation into a higher-dimensional ambient space where one can select a structured subset whose typical elements exhibit lower empirical entropy or lower structural uncertainty. In this article we develop an SST framework for graphs. We consider the set of simple undirected labeled graphs with N nodes and Ar edges, and we show that there exists a subset S ⊂ G N+k,Ar such that (i) |S| = |G N,Ar |, and (ii) the average graph entropycomputed under a specified structural entropy functional-over S is strictly smaller than the corresponding average over G N,Ar. The result highlights an important principle: in graph compression and graph computation, structural regularity can dominate raw dimensionality. We conclude by discussing practical consequences for graph storage, fast traversal, similarity-based encoding, and downstream computational pipelines such as large-scale network analytics and learning on graphs.

title: Development Resilience as a Missing State Variable for the Age of AI: Empirical Evidence and Implications for GDP and Sovereign Risk

detail.title: Development Resilience as a Missing State Variable for the Age of AI: Empirical Evidence and Implications for GDP and Sovereign Risk
detail.abstract: GDP and sovereign CDS spreads are the twin anchors of macro-financial analysis. Both are rigorously constructed. Both share a common blind spot: neither incorporates development resilience, the capacity of society's human and institutional foundations to sustain economic activity without converting stress into persistent damage. In the AI era, this gap becomes critical: AI potentially enables output growth with diminishing human participation, systematically decoupling production from the social foundations that make it durable. To measure this decoupling, this paper introduces the Development Resilience Factor (DRF ∈ (0,1]) as the omitted structural state variable and proposes two resilience-based adjustments: Gross Domestic Human Progress (GDHP = GDP × DRF), which resilience-adjusts output, and the Human Development Spread (HDS = CDS + (1-DRF) × CDS), as proposed in the earlier paper (Bhagavatula, 2026). Using G20 data, we provide empirical evidence for the relevance of DRF: it strongly explains political stability, social outcomes, and sovereign spread variation, while nominal GDP explains essentially none. DRF may be a useful state variable for monitoring resilience risk in macro-financial analysis, particularly in the AI era, when output and human foundations may increasingly diverge.

detail.abstract: Since its inception, information systems (IS) research has recognized that subconscious psychology influences technology use. Our study extends the fragmented literature regarding attachment styles and human-computer interaction (HCI), analyzing how early psychological attachment styles affect attitudes toward various technologies. We theorize that attachment styles formed in the formative years of one's life universally shape attitudes toward technology in adulthood by building on the premises that technologies are socio-technical systems, and that psychological schemas influence everyday interactions through the mechanism of transference. We examine how attachment styles are linked with trust and obsessive tendencies across smartphones, social media, generative AI, video gaming, online dating, and driverless vehicles. Our analysis reveals that avoidant attachment is consistently associated with mistrust, while anxious attachment is consistently associated with obsessive technology use. These results highlight attachment styles as key predictors of trust and engagement with technology and contributes to IS, HCI, and attachment theory literature.

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the role of layering in the architecture of money and payment systems and how recent technological innovations affect it. Layering in payments, whereby payment ledgers are hierarchical to each other, and senior ledgers allow for interoperability between junior ledgers, has historically emerged from efficiency, risk management, and governance considerations. The paper develops a framework to classify ledger hierarchies and types of payment ledgers and uses it to assess innovations including central bank digital currencies, instant payment systems, public blockchains, tokenized multi-asset platforms, expanded access of non-bank payment service providers to central bank accounts, and stablecoins. The analysis shows that many innovations do not eliminate layering but instead reorganize it, often preserving the fundamental tiered structure in which central bank money anchors the monetary system. Innovations should normally improve payment efficiency but also introduce new risks and policy challenges that must be addressed, implying the need for regulatory modernization and an evolving role for central banks in shaping payment architectures and safeguarding the singleness of money.

title: Female Leadership and the Market for Representation

detail.title: Female Leadership and the Market for Representation
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether female executive leadership reshapes the gender composition of municipal bureaucracies through discretionary appointment power. I study close mayoral elections in Brazil between female and male candidates and link electoral outcomes to individual-level campaign donation records and administrative employment data covering the universe of formal public-sector jobs. When a female candidate narrowly wins, campaign donors become more likely to enter municipal public employment. The effect is substantially larger for women: female donors experience a 27% increase relative to baseline, whereas male donors experience a 15% increase. These gains concentrate in discretionary municipal appointments and in higher-ranking professional and managerial positions. At the municipality level, female victories increase the female share among managers without expanding overall donor penetration, indicating a shift in authority rather than broad patronage capture. I find no evidence of declining qualifications or donation-size gradients consistent with a transactional exchange. The results suggest that executive discretion over hiring provides a channel through which women's electoral representation can rebalance gender representation in senior bureaucratic roles.

title: Who Bears the Cost of Devaluation? Price Dynamics and Welfare Impacts During Bolivia's 2024-2025 Currency Crisis

detail.title: Who Bears the Cost of Devaluation? Price Dynamics and Welfare Impacts During Bolivia's 2024-2025 Currency Crisis
detail.abstract: This paper dissects the asymmetric price and welfare consequences of Bolivia's de facto 60% exchange rate devaluation using high-frequency scanner data from a national supermarket chain covering January 2024 to January 2025. Despite no formal float, consumer prices rose by 15% on average-with imported goods jumping 16.8% and domestically produced goods lagging at 9.2%. The inflation burden fell unevenly across the income distribution. While the cost of high-income households' consumption baskets increased more in nominal terms (17.6%), their superior substitution elasticity allowed them to limit welfare losses to 10.9% by reallocating expenditure toward cheaper or newly available alternatives. In contrast, low-income households faced smaller nominal price increases (14.5%) but larger welfare losses (13.4%), owing to low substitutability and consumption patterns anchored to essential imported staples with few domestic substitutes. To quantify these effects, we estimate a nested CES demand model and decompose the cost-of-living impact into four channels: (i) marginal cost pass-through, (ii) retail markup adjustments, (iii) substitution across varieties, and (iv) variety entry and exit. We find that poor households face near-complete cost transmission with negligible markup relief or substitution escape routes, while rich households enjoy strategic price shielding through all three compensatory channels. Microsimulations combining our cost-of-living estimates with the 2023 household survey indicate that the devaluation increases the poverty headcount by 2.6 to 3.8 percentage points and raises the Gini coefficient by up to 0.7 points. These findings underscore a general principle: in segmented economies where the poor depend on essential imports and face low substitution elasticities, devaluation can simultaneously be inflationary and inequality-enhancing-even in the absence of formal price liberalization.

detail.abstract:
This paper evaluates the institutional design and welfare implications of the lump-sum payment option introduced in the Spanish public pension system as an incentive for delayed retirement. The analysis examines whether the lump sum, informally known as the "cheque" in administrative communications, constitutes an actuarially fair alternative to the life annuity supplement it replaces. To this end, the paper employs an integrated framework combining actuarial valuation, survival-based probabilistic analysis, heterogeneous time preferences, policy risk, and welfare evaluation under the expected utility criterion. From a comparative perspective, the Spanish design differs from the prevailing approach in advanced public pension systems, where delayed retirement incentives are primarily implemented through actuarially adjusted lifetime annuity benefits. 
The results show that the lump sum systematically deviates from actuarial neutrality and provides a lower expected value than the annuity for most of the profiles analyzed. While heterogeneity in time preference can rationalize lump-sum selection for certain segments of the distribution, particularly among lower-income retirees, the structural actuarial gap remains pronounced for middle-and high-income profiles and for individuals with longer expected longevity, especially women. In this context, the lump-sum payment may constitute a false choice: an option that formally expands flexibility but does not represent an actuarially equivalent alternative under neutral actuarial assumptions. These findings underscore the central role of actuarial neutrality and transparency in the design of delayed retirement incentives.

title: Recovering Individual Labor Earnings from Household Consumption: A Collective Model Approach with an Application to the Sahel G5

detail.title: Recovering Individual Labor Earnings from Household Consumption: A Collective Model Approach with an Application to the Sahel G5
detail.abstract: In the Sahel G5 countries-Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania, and Niger-household surveys collect detailed consumption expenditure data but individual labor earnings are either absent, plagued by massive item nonresponse, or contain implausible values. This paper addresses two linked challenges: (i) recovering total household labor income from consumption data via the household budget constraint, and (ii) allocating that householdlevel aggregate to individual workers. We ground the allocation problem in the collective household model (Chiappori, 1988, 1992), which provides a theoretically consistent sharing rule for distributing household labor income among employed members. The sharing rule depends not only on predicted earnings-as in simple proportional allocation-but also on distribution factors that affect intrahousehold bargaining power, including spousal education and age gaps, polygamy, and local sex ratios. We combine this framework with grouped-data estimation of Mincer equations (Deaton, 1985) and machine learning methods (Random Forests and Gradient Boosting Machines) to estimate latent wage structures from household-level intensive-form data. We validate the approach using the 2019 Bolivian Household Survey, where both consumption and individual earnings are observed, employing formal distributional tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics, Gini coefficient comparisons, and quantile analysis). The collective sharing rule significantly outperforms simple proportional allocation in recovering the observed earnings distribution. Applying the method to the Sahel G5, we find average returns to schooling ranging from 5% (Mauritania) to 10% (Burkina Faso), with women exhibiting significantly higher returns to education but lower returns to experience than men. Sectoral and regional segmentation patterns account for a substantial share of earnings variance. These estimates provide baseline labor earnings data for microsimulations of fiscal policy, climate adaptation, and structural transformation in one of the world's poorest regions.

detail.abstract:
Online gaming has grown from simple recreational activity into a vast, algorithmically engineered digital ecosystem that shapes human behaviour through immersive design, reward uncertainty, social hierarchies, and habit-forming engagement structures. With more than three billion active players globally and problematic gaming prevalence estimated at 6–12% among youth, the issue has moved from marginal concern to public health priority.

This paper presents a comprehensive socio-psychological framework for understanding how immersive gaming environments interact with psychological characteristics across age groups, with particular sensitivity during adolescence. Drawing from behavioural psychology, developmental science, media studies, historical analysis, and emotional intelligence research, the paper identifies core engagement mechanisms including variable reward schedules, identity attachment, social hierarchy dynamics, habit-forming routines, and circadian disruption.

Three original theoretical contributions are advanced. First, a dual-loop reinforcement model distinguishes stimulation-driven engagement — linked to sensory intensity and emotional arousal — from uncertainty-driven engagement — linked to probabilistic rewards and anticipation. Second, a multi-dimensional game taxonomy classifies games across environment, energy type, player count, and money involvement, introducing the physical energy thesis — that games requiring bodily effort preserve sportsmanship, while games requiring none allow entry without spirit — and the solo-AI danger thesis, which identifies single-player machine-mediated gaming as the highest-risk configuration. Third, a monetization corruption curve traces how gambling, as distinct from prize-based reward, systematically destroys the sportsmanship inherent in any game across historical eras.

A central preventive argument proposes that Emotional Quotient (EQ) development, rather than exclusive focus on intellectual achievement, is the most sustainable protection against digital addiction. The paper demonstrates that high-IQ individuals with low EQ are paradoxically among the most vulnerable to structured reward systems, possessing the analytical capacity to optimize their engagement while lacking the emotional architecture to feel the relational and social costs of their choices.

By shifting focus from individual blame to system-level interaction, this work contributes to interdisciplinary discussions on digital well-being across the lifespan and offers a structured foundation for future empirical research and policy development.

The cryptocurrency exchange data was sourced from BitMEX; the author has no affiliation with or interest in that exchange.

detail.abstract: This thesis reports on the applicability of drift-diffusion and diffusion-only models to estimate future price directions from Level-1 limit order book data. We fit and evaluate the probability models on a data set of 78M order book updates (1 month) of the Bitcoin − U.S. Dollar market on BitMEX, a large cryptocurrency exchange. We show that diffusion-only models outperform drift-diffusion models, which is likely a result of the limited Level-1 description of the order book. Both types of models offer significant improvements over baseline models that do not incorporate order book information. On selected evaluation points leading up to price changes, the best-performing model obtains an RMS direction prediction error of 9.18 − 30.52%. A model-based price direction classifier obtains an average classification precision on the same points in the range of 93.83 − 99.64%. We finally demonstrate effectiveness of the classifier in a simple trading strategy, resulting in an average return of 0.062% per trade and win rate of 69.12% over 38K trades. A realistic implementation of the strategy will require further analysis in price move sizes and/or limit order execution. Keywords: Drift-diffusion, cryptocurrency, exit problems, high-frequency trading, limit order books, market microstructure, option valuation.

title: Adaptive Preferences, Endogenous Returns, and the Failure of the Second Welfare Theorem

detail.title: Adaptive Preferences, Endogenous Returns, and the Failure of the Second Welfare Theorem
detail.abstract: We study a production economy in which preferences are endogenous. In an overlapping-generations model with Cobb-Douglas technology and log utility, agents update a patience parameter in response to experienced returns on capital. When return signals differ systematically across groups-due to informational frictions, institutional barriers, or market segmentation-preferences diverge endogenously even from identical initial conditions. We establish five results. First, the adaptive steady state generically differs from the social planner's optimum; the economy converges to a capital stock pinned by the reference return, not by the planner's Euler equation.

title: Crisis Narratives and Judicial Enforcement: Evidence from the Greek Fiscal Crisis

detail.title: Crisis Narratives and Judicial Enforcement: Evidence from the Greek Fiscal Crisis
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether crisis narratives affect how the judiciary handles tax evasion. We study this question in the context of the Greek debt crisis, in which tax evasion was publicly blamed for the fiscal collapse, and judges themselves experienced substantial salary cuts as part of the resulting austerity programme. Using a novel dataset compiled from Greek Supreme Court rulings between 2006 and 2014, we compare tax evasion appeals with appeals in other serious crimes not directly related to the fiscal crisis, such as homicide and rape, in a difference-indifferences framework. We find that the probability that the Supreme Court rejects tax-evasion appeals increases by about 25 percentage points relative to these control offences after January 2010-about a 43% increase relative to the pre-crisis baseline. Effects are larger in months with greater public attention to tax evasion, as measured by Google Trends, suggesting a role for salience. Our findings suggest that crisis narratives, particularly when coupled with personal economic shocks to judges, can influence the judicial treatment of tax offences.

title: Changing the Flag Over the Single Point of Failure: A Framework for a Plurilateral Critical Minerals Agreement That Achieves Genuine North American Supply Chain Resilience

detail.abstract:
The United States possesses a generational opportunity. A well-designed plurilateral critical minerals agreement is among the most powerful instruments available to advance all four objectives the November 2025 National Security Strategy assigns highest priority: securing critical mineral supply chains, reindustrializing the American economy, revitalizing the defense industrial base, and achieving energy dominance. This submission argues that realizing that opportunity requires one foundational design insight — supply chains built on partners who have compelling economic reasons to sustain the system are durable; supply chains built on contingent compliance are not.

Canada is the indispensable partner. It supplies approximately 60% of U.S. crude oil imports, the majority of U.S. electricity imports, and hosts the Ring of Fire — one of the most strategically significant critical minerals deposits in the democratic world, containing the vanadium, titanium, scandium, and gallium that Project Vault, Pax Silica, and the USGS 2025 Critical Minerals List prioritize. Canada's NORAD partnership and Five Eyes integration make its supply chain commitments qualitatively different from any other producer's. No agreement designed to achieve genuine Western Hemisphere supply chain resilience can succeed without Canada's durable participation, and Canada's durable participation requires terms under which it has a genuine, sustained economic interest in the system's success.

China's dominance in gallium (98%), rare earth elements (85%), graphite processing (80%), and titanium metal (75%) is a refinement problem, not a raw materials problem. An agreement that redirects mineral flows away from Chinese processors but concentrates value-added returns in a single allied jurisdiction does not solve the problem — it merely changes the flag flying over the single point of failure. Distributed allied processing capacity, anchored in Canada's near-zero-carbon electricity grid, is the structural correction that genuine supply chain resilience requires. Canada's clean electricity endowment — Manitoba and Quebec at near-zero carbon intensity, Ontario's nuclear-hydroelectric grid — makes electricity-intensive processing stages economically and strategically optimal in Canada rather than on the constrained U.S. grid that the administration's own AI Action Plan identifies as a binding constraint on American technological dominance.

Nine design recommendations address value-added processing incentives, allied routing continuity, Indigenous partnership as a supply-chain durability standard, protection of allied sovereign investment instruments from challenge under the agreement's own provisions, a multilateral data governance framework built on judicial authorization in the originating jurisdiction, standards-based preferential access architecture, continental defense industrial integration, distributed processing capacity development, and a formal North American Critical Minerals Processing Corridor for Ring of Fire minerals.

title: Adaptive Preferences, Social Filters, and the Political Economy of Gendered Inequality

detail.title: Adaptive Preferences, Social Filters, and the Political Economy of Gendered Inequality
detail.abstract: We develop a dynamic general-equilibrium model in which gender inequality is selfreinforcing through endogenous preference formation. In an overlapping-generations economy, agents update an aspiration parameter governing their saving behavior based on gender-specific return signals: men observe the true market return while women observe a discounted signal reflecting structural disadvantage. We derive six formal results. First, even from identical initial conditions, biased signals generate persistent preference divergence between men and women. Second, this preference gap translates into widening wealth inequality. Third, under exogenous discrimination, a unique asymmetric steady state exists in which women's aspirations are trapped at a low level. Fourth-our central result-when discrimination intensity responds endogenously to female participation, multiple equilibria emerge: a low-participation trap and a highparticipation equilibrium coexist, separated by an unstable tipping point. Fifth, removing bias after prolonged inequality produces hysteresis, with the preference gap decaying at rate ρ n per generation. Sixth, pure redistribution cannot close the gap when return signals remain biased. Calibrated simulations illustrate how economies with identical fundamentals diverge into high versus low female participation paths depending on initial conditions, and show that combined interventions targeting both returns and aspirations outperform either alone. The results formalize how structural disadvantage becomes internalized in preferences, providing a theoretical foundation for understanding why gender gaps persist despite formal legal equality.

title: AI & AI Related Procurement in 2026: Re-Engineering Vendor Contracts for Algorithmic Risk

detail.title: AI & AI Related Procurement in 2026: Re-Engineering Vendor Contracts for Algorithmic Risk

keywords: Data Ownership vs. Model Training Rights

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has moved beyond being an experimental business tool. In 2026, it has become part of everyday operational systems. Organizations are no longer just licensing software, they are adopting systems that learn from data, evolve over time, and influence decisions that can have legal or financial consequences. This shift creates a new category of exposure (algorithmic risk) that traditional SaaS contracts were not designed to address. This Article contends that AI or AI related procurement necessitates a structural re-engineering of vendor contract architecture. Legacy provisions governing data ownership, confidentiality, liability, audit rights, and regulatory compliance are inadequate when applied to continuously evolving models, layered sub-processor ecosystems, and automated decision systems subject to increasing statutory scrutiny. Drawing from emerging regulatory frameworks in both the United States and the European Union, this Article identifies multiple contractual domains that procurement and legal teams must recalibrate to mitigate algorithmic harms and allocate risk coherently. Its central argument is both practical and forward-looking: accountability for AI systems should be built into contracts at the time they are negotiated, rather than addressed later through regulatory action or lawsuits.

title: Dynamic Signaling and Preemption in the Middle East Conflict

detail.title: Dynamic Signaling and Preemption in the Middle East Conflict
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the escalation of the Middle East conflict, specifically the retaliatory cycles between the United States, Israel, and Iran, through the lens of game-theoretic models under incomplete information. By integrating Jean Tirole's frameworks on reputational capital and preemption timing, we demonstrate how the necessity to defend "reputational assets" for future deterrence compels actors to engage in suboptimal escalation. Furthermore, the model explains how asymmetric information regarding resolve leads to a "race to preempt," where military actions are accelerated to signal strength. The analysis concludes that the conflict is driven by a rational yet tragic calculus where the pursuit of long-term deterrence results in the dissipation of strategic rents and inevitable escalation.

detail.abstract: This paper articulates the integrated analytical relationship between the Psychoeconomic Resilience Model (PRM) and the Systemic Influence & Resilience Index™ (SIRX™) as a unified research architecture for observing decision integrity in complex institutional systems. The paper does not introduce an additional model or advance a governance prescription. title: Galle v Rauh: Comparing Two Revenue Estimates for California Billionaire Taxation
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Accounting Area

detail.title: Galle v Rauh: Comparing Two Revenue Estimates for California Billionaire Taxation
detail.abstract: California is considering a one-time tax on the wealth of billionaires. Two recent reports attempt to estimate the fiscal effects of the proposal. One, by Galle, Gamage, Saez, and Shanske (2026), provides the primary estimate cited by supporters of the policy. Another, by Rauh, Jaros, Kearney, Doran, and Cosso (2026), offers a much lower estimate and a broader analysis of fiscal consequences. Galle et al. estimate the tax will produce 2.5 times more revenue than Rauh et al, and Rauh et al. find that the total fiscal impact of the law may be negative. This note compares the methodology used in the two reports. Galle et al. rely on a simple static calculation based on Forbes estimates of billionaire wealth and assume that 10 percent of the tax base will be avoided. Rauh et al., in contrast, construct the tax base on a person-by-person basis, adjust the Forbes list for residency, incorporate evidence of migration from the literature, consider a wider range of behavioral responses drawn from the wealth-tax literature, and examine the fiscal consequences of lost income-tax revenue if high-wealth individuals leave the state. These methodological differences explain why the two reports arrive at dramatically different conclusions.

title: Does Firm-Specific Political Risk Exacerbate Climate Change Exposure? Insights from a Text-based Analysis
affiliations: NIDA Business School, National Institute of Development Administration (NIDA), Pennsylvania State University - School of Graduate Professional Studies (SGPS), Mahidol University International College (MUIC) and Sasin GIBA

detail.title: Does Firm-Specific Political Risk Exacerbate Climate Change Exposure? Insights from a Text-based Analysis
detail.abstract:
Purpose: This study examines the effect of firm-specific political risk on climate change exposure, focusing on how political risk exacerbates climate vulnerabilities, particularly through regulatory uncertainties.

Design/methodology/approach: The research utilizes a text-based analysis, employing metrics derived from advanced textual analysis and machine learning algorithms. A large sample of U.S. firms is analyzed to assess the impact of political risk on climate change exposure. Various robustness checks, including propensity score matching, entropy balancing, and instrumental-variable analysis, are conducted to ensure the reliability of the findings.

Findings: The results demonstrate that higher political risk leads to greater climate change exposure, particularly in the context of regulatory risks. Additionally, the study reveals that climate change exposure driven by political risk negatively affects firm value, indicating that political instability undermines market valuations by increasing climate-related vulnerabilities.

Practical implications

The findings carry several important implications for corporate managers, investors, and policymakers. Managers should integrate political risk assessment into their climate risk management frameworks, strengthening governance and investing in adaptive capabilities such as R&D to mitigate vulnerability. Investors should evaluate firms’ political and environmental risk exposures jointly, as political instability can amplify climate-related risks and depress firm value. For policymakers, the results highlight the importance of regulatory stability and policy coherence to encourage sustained corporate investment in climate resilience. A predictable policy environment can reduce uncertainty, promote long-term planning, and enhance overall market confidence.

Originality: This research contributes to the literature by examining the effect of firm-specific political risk on climate change exposure, using innovative text-based metrics. The study provides new insights into how political risks exacerbate climate vulnerabilities and impact firm value, highlighting the need for integrated risk management strategies that address both political and environmental challenges.

title: Pricing Mechanism of Regional Forestry Carbon Credits: A Supply-Demand Perspective
affiliations: Changzhou Institute of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Nanjing Forestry University, College of Economics & Management

detail.title: Pricing Mechanism of Regional Forestry Carbon Credits: A Supply-Demand Perspective
detail.abstract: Revealing the formation mechanism of regional forestry carbon sequestration prices is critical for optimizing forest horizontal ecological compensation standards and strengthening incentives for forest ecological acceptance areas, thereby promoting coordinated regional development. This study integrates the SBM model, the forestry carbon sequestration cost model, and the Rubinstein bargaining model to estimate the equilibrium price in the forestry carbon sequestration market. The main findings are as follows: (1) From 2012 to 2021, the estimated average marginal carbon abatement costs across districts and counties in Chongqing range from 696.73 to 1,178.21 CNY/t, with an overall average of 964.31 CNY/t. (2) Using data from forestry carbon sequestration projects in Chongqing and a carbon sequestration supply model, the average carbon sequestration cost of forestry is estimated at 484.13 CNY/t. (3) Given clearly defined regional carbon abatement costs and forestry carbon sequestration costs, the equilibrium market price of forestry carbon sequestration is 964.31 CNY/t when forest ecological acceptance areas are sufficiently patient or when forest ecological payment areas exhibit no patience. When forest ecological acceptance areas exhibit no patience and forest ecological payment areas have a patience level of 0.5, the bargaining surplus is equally shared between the two parties, resulting in an equilibrium forestry carbon sequestration price of 724.22 CNY/t. Overall, these findings provide an operational pricing basis for incorporating carbon sequestration values into existing forest horizontal ecological compensation practices and refining compensation standards, while also offering empirical support for market-oriented trading mechanisms in ecological compensation.

title: The Pause: Four Mechanical Failures of Money.

detail.abstract: Modern monetary systems fail not primarily through corruption or mismanagement, but through structural design flaws that detach money from enduring proof, compress responsibility across time, privilege early access to issuance, and concentrate capital toward existing centres of power. These mechanics systematically reward proximity, speed, and abstraction over real value creation and stewardship, producing predictable cycles of extraction, inequality, reductionism and erosion of trust.

title: Client-Bank Surplus in Structured Products: A Theoretical Index

detail.title: Client-Bank Surplus in Structured Products: A Theoretical Index
detail.abstract: Structured products marketed to retail and wealth management clients often involve opaque pricing and potential conflicts of interest between issuing banks and investors. This paper introduces a simple client-bank surplus index that decomposes the expected economic value created by a structured product transaction between the two parties. Using a discrete-state model, we define the client surplus as the difference between the product's fair value and its asset price, and the bank surplus as the difference between the issue price and the bank's hedging cost.

title: Bridging the Accountability Gap in F-1 Compliance Verification: An IoT-Enabled Platform for Hybrid and Extended SEVP-Certified Institutional Contexts

detail.title: Bridging the Accountability Gap in F-1 Compliance Verification: An IoT-Enabled Platform for Hybrid and Extended SEVP-Certified Institutional Contexts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a conceptual design study based on regulatory analysis and publicly available federal data. No human participants were involved. Ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Federal regulations under 8 CFR 214.2(f) mandate verifiable physical presence for all F-1 visa holders maintaining full-time enrollment status. Yet across the 8,744 institutions holding SEVP certification, attendance verification remains predominantly reliant on analog methods, paper sign-in sheets, photographs, and manual attestations that lack the audit trails required for compliance reviews. This "Accountability Gap" is most acute among the estimated 250-350 SEVP-certified institutions operating hybrid or low-residency programs, where geographically dispersed students, compressed residency sessions, and satellite campus operations eliminate the ambient presence indicators available in traditional campus settings. This paper presents a conceptual design study grounded in regulatory analysis, publicly available federal enforcement data, and scenario-based financial modeling. The proposed system, E-College, is a cross-platform mobile application integrating Internet of Things (IoT) technologies including Near Field Communication (NFC) for proximity authentication, geofencing for dwell-time validation, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for location intelligence, and biometric verification architected to generate cryptographically signed, audit-ready attendance records termed "Trusted Data Points" (TDPs). Developed using React Native with a Node.js backend, the platform is designed to produce FERPA-compliant, SEVP-exportable compliance documentation aligned with the specific regulatory requirements of hybrid F-1 programs. The platform has been developed but has not yet undergone field validation; the study establishes the theoretical, regulatory, and architectural foundations for future implementation and empirical testing. Sensitivity analysis across nine operational scenarios projects baseline annual logistics savings of $23,620 per institution and payback periods of 12-18 months. Predictive modeling using logistic regression suggests potential for 15-20% improvements in student retention through early attrition detection. A STRIDE-based threat model and FERPA-aligned security architecture address IoT-specific vulnerabilities including proxy authentication, data tampering, and geolocation spoofing. Competitive landscape analysis confirms that no existing commercial platform provides integrated F-1 compliance verification combining NFC proximity, geofencing dwell-time, biometric identity, and SEVIS-compatible (batch XML format-compatible) export for hybrid program contexts. The paper further analyzes the platform’s scalability to the broader SEVP-certified institutional ecosystem including ESL programs, traditional universities, and vocational schools and proposes a phased research roadmap for empirical validation. The findings contribute to educational technology, regulatory compliance automation, and institutional risk management literature.

title: Health Information Systems (His) Integration and Interoperability Frameworks

detail.title: Health Information Systems (His) Integration and Interoperability Frameworks
detail.abstract: Modern healthcare increasingly depends on digital information systems to support clinical workflows, patient data management, and organizational decision-making. However, the effectiveness of these systems is often limited by fragmentation and the inability of different platforms to exchange data seamlessly. This study examines Health Information Systems (HIS) integration and interoperability frameworks and evaluates their role in enabling efficient healthcare data exchange and coordinated care delivery. Using a structured literature synthesis approach, the research analyzes interoperability standards such as HL7 and Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), integration architectures, and the role of emerging technologies including artificial intelligence and Internet-of-Things-based healthcare infrastructures. The findings suggest that interoperability significantly improves patient care coordination, data accessibility, and healthcare operational efficiency. Despite these benefits, healthcare institutions continue to face challenges related to technological compatibility, regulatory compliance, and data governance. The study concludes that implementing standardized interoperability frameworks and scalable integration architectures is essential for building resilient and patient-centered digital healthcare ecosystems.

title: Theory of the Resistive Capital Gradient

detail.title: Theory of the Resistive Capital Gradient
detail.abstract: Traditional finance assumes that capital is an active seeker of the highest returns. This paper proposes an alternative view: the theory of the Resistive Capital Gradient (RCG) which posits that capital flows to where it encounters the least resistance. By shifting the focus from the motivation of the investor to the physics of the transmission, I introduce 'Impedance' (Ω) as the primary determinant of capital flow. This framework provides a mechanical explanation for why liquidity often 'shunts' into low-resistance financial assets rather than high-resistance productive sectors, explaining the persistent failure of stimulus to reach the real economy. This 'shunting' effect provides a mechanical explanation for the observed inverted-U relationship between financial development and growth identified in recent international metropolitan analyses (Ioannou & Wójcik, 2021), where excessive financial size eventually correlates with declining economic returns. The framework also explains flows 'uphill' from developing to advanced nations and can stagnate even amidst massive liquidity injections. The paper concludes with a falsifiable theoretical proposition: the multiplier effect of any stimulus is inversely proportional to the Impedance of the target sector. A companion policy tool, the Price Restraint and Investment Compliance Index (PRICI), is presented as a mechanism to directly lower Ω and restore the transmission of capital to productive uses. This working paper proposes the framework and identifies key empirical tests required for validation, inviting formal theoretical development and rigorous empirical investigation by the research community.

title: Title IV-D Performance Incentives and Shared Parenting Outcomes: A Policy Analysis

detail.title: Title IV-D Performance Incentives and Shared Parenting Outcomes: A Policy Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none

detail.abstract: Title IV-D of the Social Security Act (1975) funds state child support enforcement through federal matching of administrative costs and performance incentives allocated from a capped national pool tied to five metrics. The program has been effective in increasing paternity establishment rates above 90% and generating more than $30 billion in annual collections. However, the structure of the incentive system could create financial pressures affecting custody policy and child support guideline design. The review considers the historical development of Title IV-D, the structure of its performance incentives, data from variations across states, and procedural critiques from legal scholarship. I assess policy options, considering their feasibility and potential impact on shared parenting arrangements. Recalibrating incentives and strengthening proportional support guidelines may better align program objectives with contemporary family structures

title: Ambition Meets Reality: Pinhas Lavon's Animal-protein Plan under Austerity and Rationing in Israel, 1950-1951
affiliations: Ariel University - Department of Economics and Business Administration and Ashkelon Academic College

detail.title: Ambition Meets Reality: Pinhas Lavon's Animal-protein Plan under Austerity and Rationing in Israel, 1950-1951
detail.abstract: In April 1949, the Israeli government introduced the austerity and rationing regime to ensure the equitable distribution of basic foods during a period of war, mass immigration and severe financial strain. The Minister of Supply and Rationing, Dov Yosef, was responsible for administering food supply and the austerity and rationing regime. In November 1950, the Ministry of Supply and Rationing was dismantled, and Pinhas Lavon, the new Minister of Agriculture, replaced Yosef as the minister responsible for food supply, austerity and rationing. Lavon reoriented the austerity food policy framework in two ways: a. from cracking down on the black market and insisting that the current rations are nutritionally adequate, to relaxing anti-black market enforcement and increasing rations to improve nutrition; b. from exclusive concern with nutritional value while neglecting psychological considerations, to significant concern for psychological considerations. This paper quantitatively evaluates Pinhas Lavon's ambitious plan to raise per capita daily animal protein consumption to 38g in 1951, vs. 33g under Yosef's original plan. The analysis draws on extensive archival materials, including newly collected monthly data on animal protein consumption and official supplies of animal-source foods. We find that Lavon's plan mostly failed: Daily per capita animal protein consumption declined from 31g to 30g, monthly beef rations averaged 598g vs. Lavon's 750g target, monthly beef sausage rations averaged 23g vs. Lavon's 350g target, and milk bread failed due to a combination of kosher and quality problems. However, standard milk-a blend of 75%-100% fresh milk and 0%-25% reconstituted milk-succeeded after Lavon left office: It made possible the derationing of milk in April 1952, and in 1952-1953, it contributed up to 22% of the 5g additional protein in Lavon's plan vs. Yosef's original plan. Lavon's efforts to import beef were hampered by circumstances beyond his control, including declining foreign currency reserves, skyrocketing global commodity prices and shipping costs due to the Korean War, one of the worst droughts in Israel's history and arbitrary Finance Ministry decisions. On the other hand, Lavon did make several avoidable policy errors: overoptimism regarding his ability to supply a 350g monthly sausage ration, the arbitrary decision to roll out milk bread nationwide despite its known kosher and quality problems, and failure to fix the dysfunctional food distribution system.

title: Why Foreign Exchange Risk Is the Primary Deal Killer in U.S.-Africa Transactions

detail.title: Why Foreign Exchange Risk Is the Primary Deal Killer in U.S.-Africa Transactions
detail.abstract: Foreign exchange risk is often described as one of several challenges in U.S.–Africa cross-border investment. In practice, it is frequently the factor that determines whether a transaction closes or fails after closing. This paper argues that foreign exchange risk is not inherently prohibitive but is consistently misunderstood, mispriced, and assigned to the wrong party in small and mid-sized transactions. Drawing on institutional research and transaction-level analysis, the paper explains how currency mismatch can turn operationally sound businesses into financially distressed borrowers, why conventional hedging and development finance tools rarely reach smaller deals, and how structural misalignment rather than capital scarcity drives repeated transaction failure. The analysis concludes that treating foreign exchange exposure as a primary structuring variable is necessary for sustainable U.S.–Africa investment and for aligning private capital with long-term economic development.

title: Tangible Boundaries: Embodied Externalization for Affect Regulation in Trauma

detail.title: Tangible Boundaries: Embodied Externalization for Affect Regulation in Trauma

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n.a.
declarations.ethicsApproval: n.a.
